title: Reply note before carried posts on reconnect, restore the hookless launch note, and finish the held-chat cue
body:
Review findings on commits afc3660 and 4934798 (read both bodies, then docs/remote-sessions.md). Two independent reviews (code, design) found no loss or duplication in the hold itself but these defects. The human's standing requirement: production-ready and PROVEN by driving the real application; reproduce each behavioural defect BEFORE the fix, fix it, verify AFTER, and record both. Use the same procedure, run-log format and BEFORE/AFTER tables as commit 4934798 (its card: `foreman kanban list jmz2w2 --json`; reuse its setup paragraph verbatim: own release build in target/agent/hooks, config dir target/agent/appdata-s2hp4s, own pipe, test Remote andy@192.168.8.168 key login, new never-trusted /tmp directory per run, clean up everything you created, never stop a foreman by name, never print a token in the repo). When reading a transcript, count typed prompts AND queued_command attachments.
Blocked by: Hold every hookable Remote Claude, and show and release a held chat

1. Reconnect delivers carried posts before the fresh reply note. wm.rs reconnect calls fresh.queue_injects_front(old.take_pending_injects()) after attach_tunnel queued the typed note, so posts queued on the dead connection reach a resumed held Claude BEFORE the note that teaches the new token; it answers them with the dead token (401). For a resumed hookless agent the carried posts go through pending_inject directly and arrive with no note at all. Fix: on any reconnect the agent learns the new token before, or together with, the first thing it is asked to answer; exactly one note per connection; order of the carried posts kept; ReplyNote::strip still removes the dead connection's note. Reproduce live: get a post queued for a Remote Claude that cannot take it yet (for example post to it while it is busy or held), kill its ssh, `foreman reconnect`, and see which token its reply uses (the room shows the reply or does not). Also one hookless case (Codex on the Remote, no hook-trust bypass flag; if its sandbox blocks the curl, show from its transcript which command it tried).
2. Hookless agents that are not Claude lost their reply route. 4934798 moved the typed launch note to the first chat post for EVERY hookless agent. The proven failure (the note's Enter answering a trust dialog with "No, exit") is Claude's. So: a hookless CLAUDE (its own --settings, any Windows Remote) keeps the note with its first post, as now. Every other hookless agent whose prompt cannot carry the note (Grok, Codex shapes prompt_index refuses such as codex exec or a one-word brief, wrapper and npx launches) goes back to the typed note at launch, as before bdf3877. One pure function decides, with a table test listing every row. Both providers' foreman-dispatch skill copies must tell a dispatcher the one remaining case where an agent cannot reply until it is posted to (hookless Claude) and what to do (post to it once). Verify live with a Codex shape that prompt_index refuses.
3. A press on the cue strip leaks into the terminal. Session::handle_mouse treats the whole content rect, strip included, as grid content, so a click on the cue (lead text or the action) also sends mouse press/release bytes to an agent with mouse reporting on, and a drag from the strip starts a selection. Reject presses inside the cue's bar the way the search bar does. Extend the existing cue test to assert no mouse bytes reach the PTY and no selection starts.
4. The cue resizes the terminal on every launch. It reserves rows, so every dispatched Claude shows it for the moment before its UserPromptSubmit and the grid shrinks then grows (two PTY resizes through ConPTY and ssh while Claude draws its startup UI, one of them just before the first held paste). Fix: the cue appears only once a hold has lasted HELD_CUE_AFTER (choose and justify a value of a few seconds from your own launch timings; a normal launch must never show it), while `status --json` chat_held stays immediate. Then prove on the real Remote that the remaining appear/disappear resize is safe: hold a Claude at its trust dialog past the threshold (cue up), answer the dialog, and confirm from snapshots and the transcript that the dialog and then the REPL are drawn correctly at both sizes and that a held post still arrives exactly once (10 runs, including 3 with a long single-line post over 4095 bytes).
5. Cue design, required by the design review (do exactly this):
 - lead text becomes "Chat waiting until {agent} is ready" and the action stays "deliver now"; the " — " separator is its own fixed, non-clickable piece so it survives truncation of the lead in a narrow pane;
 - the action is underlined at rest (1 px, th.dim) and on hover (th.text), so it does not rely on lightness alone;
 - hover tooltip on the action: "Types the waiting chat into this pane now. If {agent} is showing a prompt, answer it first.";
 - the action's hit rect is the full strip height, expanded 6 px horizontally;
 - use a non-focusable click sense so no key can ever activate it (the rule that no key press opens a hold must be structural, not a side effect of focus clearing); add a test;
 - update the cue test and the quoted text in docs/remote-sessions.md.
 Do not restyle the disconnect bar in this card.
6. parse_deliver_args builds its errors by replacing the word reconnect in another verb's message, which mangles an echoed argument. Give it its own messages.
Not in scope: a hold that never opens for claude agents / claude mcp list or when curl is missing is now visible (chat_held, cue) and has `foreman deliver`; leave it. Grok and Windows Remotes stay unverified; never mark them tested. The GUI cannot be judged from the terminal: do not claim the cue looks right; describe what the human should see.
Hard rules as before: nothing assumes foreman, its skills or hook files on the Remote; a Remote agent may post chat, read history, read status and report hook events, nothing else; existing requests byte-identical on the wire; nothing under cfg(test) spawns a process or socket outside the remote_probe network guard; no state detection from screen text; no Codex hook-trust bypass flag.
Done when:
- BEFORE and AFTER records for items 1, 2 and 4 are in the commit body and a new spec Results entry (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-20-remote-sessions-design.md), AFTER with no failures, or the card is blocked with the numbers
- unit tests pin: note-before-carried-posts on reconnect for held and hookless agents, the per-agent note table, no mouse bytes from the cue strip, the cue threshold, the non-focusable action
- docs/remote-sessions.md and both providers' dispatch skill copies (embedded-skill rebuild rule in foreman-docs-and-writing) say what is true; cite-guard clean; full suite passes
Gate: cargo test --target-dir target/agent; pwsh -File .claude/hooks/cite-guard.ps1 -All
